parsed.answer: The exact conditional probability is 7/20. Let D be the disclosure event that the auditor's uniformly chosen amber position lies in {1,2}. For any fixed mode size k, the chosen position is marginally uniform over all six positions: each position has probability k/6 of being amber and is then chosen with probability 1/k. Therefore P(D)=2/6=1/3 for every mode, so P(D)=1/3 overall. Now compute P(position 6 amber and D) by mode. Mode S1 (k=1, prior 1/4): if position 6 is amber, then the selected amber position cannot be in {1,2}, so contribution 0. Mode S2 (k=3, prior 1/2): P(position 6 amber)=3/6=1/2. Given 6 is amber, the other two amber positions are uniform among the other five; expected number among {1,2} is 2*(2/5)=4/5, so the chance the selected amber position is in {1,2} is (4/5)/3=4/15. Thus P(6 amber and D | S2)=1/2*4/15=2/15, and weighted by prior 1/2 gives 1/15. Mode S3 (k=4, prior 1/4): P(position 6 amber)=4/6=2/3. Given 6 is amber, the other three amber positions are uniform among the other five; expected number among {1,2} is 3*(2/5)=6/5, so the chance the selected amber position is in {1,2} is (6/5)/4=3/10. Thus P(6 amber and D | S3)=2/3*3/10=1/5, and weighted by prior 1/4 gives 1/20. Adding these weighted contributions gives P(6 amber and D)=1/15+1/20=7/60. Hence P(6 amber | D)=(7/60)/(1/3)=7/20. Assumptions: conditional on a mode, every subset of the stated size is equally likely; the auditor chooses uniformly among actual amber positions; and the disclosure is exactly the event D, with no extra information about which of positions 1 or 2 was selected.
